neighbours.label: Reuses a module-name fragment in a Python from-import symbol or import alias.
fire:
from graphic.vector_path import VectorPath
path = VectorPath()
from document.text_layout import TextLayout
layout = TextLayout()
from network.socket_pool import SocketPool
pool = SocketPool()
from archive.record_store import RecordStore
store = RecordStore()
from display.color_table import ColorTable
table = ColorTable()
from sensor.sample_buffer import SampleBuffer
buffer = SampleBuffer()
from image.pixel_grid import PixelGrid
grid = PixelGrid()
from editor.line_cursor import LineCursor
cursor = LineCursor()
quiet:
from graphic.curve_path import Renderer
shape = Renderer()
from document.page_layout import Formatter
page = Formatter()
from network.connection_pool import Client
connection = Client()
from archive.object_store import Repository
archive = Repository()
from display.shade_table import Palette
colors = Palette()
from sensor.reading_buffer import Collector
samples = Collector()
from image.point_grid import Canvas
picture = Canvas()
from editor.word_cursor import Marker
position = Marker()

notes: Several top examples copy a recently seen identifier fragment across an import. Probes supported some repeated imports but not all; ordinary repeated words were also inconsistent. The claim is limited to the import context and tested with new module/symbol combinations.
